subject: physics
title: Transverse and longitudinal waves
key_idea: Waves transfer **energy** and information from place to place without transferring matter. In a **transverse** wave the vibrations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer. In a **longitudinal** wave they are parallel to it.

blocks.text: This section explains what a wave moves and how we know it is the wave, and not the material, that travels.

items.meaning: A disturbance that transfers energy and information without transferring matter.
A repeated movement to and fro about a fixed position.
The material a wave travels through, such as water or air.

items: A cork floats on the surface of a pond. When ripples pass, the cork moves up and down.
The cork does not travel across the pond with the ripples.
The water particles oscillate up and down. The energy moves in the direction of the wave.
When someone claps, the air particles vibrate backwards and forwards about fixed positions.
The air does not travel from the clap to your ear. The vibrations are passed on from particle to particle.
The energy travels in the direction of the wave.
A wave transfers energy and information, not matter.
A floating cork moves up and down on ripples. It is not carried along.
Air particles vibrate in a sound wave. They do not travel with it.

blocks.text: The two types of wave are described by how the vibrations move compared with the direction the wave travels.

items.meaning: A wave in which the vibrations are perpendicular (at right angles) to the direction of energy transfer.
A wave in which the vibrations are parallel to the direction of energy transfer.
A region of a longitudinal wave where the particles are squashed together.
A region of a longitudinal wave where the particles are spread apart.

items: The wave has peaks and troughs.
Ripples on a water surface are a transverse wave. A ripple tank is used to model transverse waves.
Electromagnetic waves, such as light and radio waves, are transverse.
Seismic S-waves are transverse.
The wave has compressions and rarefactions.
Sound waves in air are longitudinal. The air particles vibrate parallel to the direction the sound travels.
Seismic P-waves are longitudinal.

checks.q: Describe the difference between transverse and longitudinal waves.
checks.a: In a transverse wave the vibrations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer. In a longitudinal wave the vibrations are parallel to the direction of energy transfer.

checks.q: A cork floats on the surface of a pond while ripples pass. Describe how the cork moves and explain what this shows.
checks.a: The cork moves up and down, perpendicular to the direction the ripples travel. It is not carried along, so the wave transfers energy but not matter.

checks.q: Complete the sentence. When sound waves travel through air they create areas of ___ and ___.

worked_example.question:
Electromagnetic waves are transverse.
Some other types of wave are longitudinal.
Describe the difference between transverse and longitudinal waves.
answer_points: In a transverse wave, the oscillations / vibrations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer.
In a longitudinal wave, the oscillations / vibrations are parallel to the direction of energy transfer.
worked_example.tip: Direction of wave travel is allowed for direction of energy transfer.

worked_example.question:
Sound waves are longitudinal waves.
Water waves are transverse waves.
Describe the difference between longitudinal waves and transverse waves.
answer_points: Longitudinal: the vibrations are parallel to the direction of travel.
Transverse: the vibrations are at right angles to the direction of travel.
The connection between the direction of travel and the direction of the vibrations is stated.
worked_example.tip: Back and forth oscillations or compressions and rarefactions are allowed for longitudinal, and up and down oscillations for transverse.

worked_example.question:
A teacher uses water waves in a ripple tank to demonstrate transverse waves.

A student tries to describe water waves in the sea.

'The water waves move up and down. The water particles move all the way across the surface of the sea. This means that water moves in the direction of the waves.'

Part of his explanation is incorrect.

Write an improved and correct description about water waves in the sea.
answer_points: The water particles move up and down (oscillate vertically), at 90° to the direction of the wave.
The energy moves in the direction of the wave.
worked_example.tip: Any two of the three points score the marks. Statements repeated from the question are ignored.
